summary: A 1982 collection of summary notes about the RFCs numbered 600 to 699. It is an informational roundup, not a specification.

eli5.summary: This is a catalog entry, like a library list, giving a short note about each of the hundred documents numbered 600 to 699.

questions: what happened in early internet rfc development
subtitle: A 1982 index of the hundredth batch of RFCs

tldr.problem: The RFC series was growing rapidly and keeping track of the recent documents had become difficult.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC publishes a summary table of RFCs 600 through 699, with one-line descriptions of each.
tldr.outcome: It serves as a historical reference for understanding the state of the Internet in the early 1980s, when many core protocols were still being refined.

today: RFC 699 is an Informational historical document. It does not describe standards or protocols that are still in use; rather, it serves as an index to documents from an earlier era of Internet development.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
RFC 699 is a summary of the 100 RFCs numbered 600 through 699. Each entry gives the RFC number, author, publication date, title and a brief note describing the document's purpose or significance.

The RFCs in this range span 1973 to 1982 and cover the early development of network protocols, including refinements to FTP, Telnet, and the NCP and IMP/Host protocols that preceded the modern TCP/IP stack.
sections.eli5: This is an old library catalog from 1982 that lists and describes 100 documents about early computer networks.

sections.title: Contents of the 600-699 Range
sections.content:
The RFCs in this range address a wide variety of topics. Some describe protocol specifications and revisions, such as improvements to the File Transfer Protocol (RFCs 640, 686, 691), Telnet options (RFCs 651-658), and IMP/Host protocol changes (RFCs 687, 690, 692). Others document the state of early networking implementations, administrative matters like host naming (RFCs 606, 608, 623, 625, 627) and IMP scheduling (RFC 622).

Several RFCs are administrative or informational: RFC 601 reports traffic statistics, RFC 619 contains round-trip time measurements, and RFC 628 discusses RFC numbering practices. A few are no longer issued, as noted in the list.
sections.eli5: The RFCs talk about how to copy files over networks, how to use terminals remotely, how computers should connect to each other, and how to name computers on a network.

sections.title: Significance and Use
sections.content:
This summary provides historical documentation of the Internet's early standardization process. The RFCs listed show the iterative refinement of protocols: authors proposed ideas, others commented and proposed alternatives, and revisions addressed concerns. Many protocols mentioned here evolved into modern standards (TCP, IP, DNS, email), while others are now obsolete.

The document is useful for anyone studying Internet history or understanding how specific protocols developed over time.
sections.eli5: By reading what people said in these old documents, you can see how the Internet grew and changed from the earliest days.
